@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+# Backfill (#2378): builds the FreeBSD package of an existing vX.Y.0 tag and
+# attaches it to that tag's GitHub release. Provenance: the build steps are
+# those of the freebsd job of release.yml (vmactions/freebsd-vm, then
+# scripts/package-freebsd.sh at the tag). It exists because the freebsd job
+# of v0.23.0 ran out of memory, and a tag is never moved to repeat a build.
+# Trigger: workflow_dispatch ONLY (AGENTS.md "GitHub Actions minutes are
+# budgeted"). Start it by hand after the tag's release is on GitHub:
+#   gh workflow run freebsd-backfill.yml -f tag=v0.23.0
+# The tagged tree is built as it is. The workflow never creates, moves or
+# pushes a tag. It never replaces an asset: a release that already has a
+# FreeBSD archive is refused, and the upload has no --clobber.
+name: FreeBSD backfill
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      tag:
+        description: 'Release tag to build, vX.Y.0 (for example v0.23.0)'
+        required: true
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  validate:
+    # The tag pattern is not a dispatch input rule, so it is checked here.
+    # The input enters the script only through env, never through a
+    # ${{ }} expression inside run:.
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    outputs:
+      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Check the tag and its release
+        id: check
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          if ! [[ "$TAG" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.0$ ]]; then
+            echo "::error::'$TAG' is not a feature tag of the form vX.Y.0"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          # Exits non-zero when the tag does not exist.
+          gh api "repos/$REPO/git/ref/tags/$TAG" --jq .object.sha >/dev/null
+          release_json=$(gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$REPO" --json assets) || {
+            echo "::error::no GitHub release exists for $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          }
+          count=$(jq -r '[.assets[].name | select(endswith("-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz"))] | length' <<<"$release_json")
+          if [ "$count" -ne 0 ]; then
+            echo "::error::the release of $TAG already has a FreeBSD archive"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "tag=$TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+  build:
+    needs: validate
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 90
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: refs/tags/${{ needs.validate.outputs.tag }}
+      - name: Build and package in FreeBSD
+        uses: vmactions/freebsd-vm@v1
+        with:
+          release: '14'
+          cpu: 3
+          # #2378: 5120 MB ran out of memory in boa_ast (exit 137). The hosted
+          # runner has 16 GB; 12288 MB leaves room for the host. -j 2 keeps
+          # the peak memory of rustc low.
+          mem: 12288
+          run: |
+            pkg install -y bash rust pkgconf libxkbcommon libX11 wayland vulkan-loader mesa-libs
+            export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/camcraft-target
+            cargo build -j 2 --locked --release -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post
+            "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/camcraft-cli" --version
+            "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/post" --version
+            CAMCRAFT_BIN_DIR="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release" bash scripts/package-freebsd.sh
+            tar -tzf dist/*-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz | grep '/camcraft-ui$'
+            tar -tzf dist/*-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz | grep '/examples/first-part.camproj$'
+      - name: Check copied archive
+        run: test -s dist/*-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: freebsd-package
+          path: dist/*-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
+  attach:
+    # The only job with write access. It runs no code from the tag: it only
+    # receives the archive that the build job uploaded.
+    needs: [validate, build]
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    permissions:
+      contents: write
+    env:
+      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+      TAG: ${{ needs.validate.outputs.tag }}
+      REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: freebsd-package
+          path: dist
+      - name: Refuse a release that already has a FreeBSD archive
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          shopt -s nullglob
+          files=(dist/*-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz)
+          if [ ${#files[@]} -ne 1 ]; then
+            echo "::error::expected one FreeBSD archive, found ${#files[@]}"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          release_json=$(gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$REPO" --json assets)
+          count=$(jq -r '[.assets[].name | select(endswith("-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz"))] | length' <<<"$release_json")
+          if [ "$count" -ne 0 ]; then
+            echo "::error::the release of $TAG already has a FreeBSD archive"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Attach the archive to the release
+        run: gh release upload "$TAG" --repo "$REPO" dist/*-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz
+      - name: Remove the 'FreeBSD did not succeed' line from the release body
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          pattern='^> Not in this release: FreeBSD \(tar\.gz\) build did not succeed '
+          gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$REPO" --json body --jq .body > body.md
+          if ! grep -q -E "$pattern" body.md; then
+            echo "The release body has no FreeBSD 'did not succeed' line; nothing to edit."
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          grep -v -E "$pattern" body.md > body-new.md || true
+          gh release edit "$TAG" --repo "$REPO" --notes-file - < body-new.md

-            cargo build --locked --release -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post
+            cargo build -j 2 --locked --release -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post

@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+## #2378 - FreeBSD package for a tag whose freebsd job ran out of memory
+
+**What was decided.** Two changes. The `freebsd` job of `release.yml` gets
+`mem: 12288` (was 5120) and runs `cargo build -j 2`. A new workflow,
+`.github/workflows/freebsd-backfill.yml`, has the trigger `workflow_dispatch`
+only. Its input `tag` names an existing `vX.Y.0` tag. It builds the tagged
+tree with the same VM steps, then attaches the archive to that tag's release.
+It refuses a release that already has a FreeBSD archive. It then removes the
+line "FreeBSD (tar.gz) build did not succeed" from the release body and
+changes nothing else.
+
+**Why.** The freebsd job of v0.23.0 was killed with exit 137 while it built
+`boa_ast`. The probable cause is memory: the VM had 5 GB. The hosted
+`ubuntu-24.04` runner has 16 GB, so 12 GB for the VM leaves room for the host.
+`-j 2` lowers the peak of rustc. A tag is never moved, so the tag run cannot
+repeat the build with a fixed workflow. A dispatch-only workflow builds the
+tagged tree and adds the missing asset to the existing release.
+
+**The build and the upload are two jobs.** The `build` job runs with
+`contents: read`. Only the `attach` job has `contents: write`, and it runs no
+code from the tag. GitHub sets permissions per job, not per step. A step
+with write access inside the build job would give the built code a write
+token. The archive passes between the jobs as a workflow artifact.
+
+**Memory value.** The vmactions/freebsd-vm README gives the default
+(6144 MB) and no maximum. 12288 MB is the value the maintainer approved.
+It is not measured. A first run may still need more or less.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- A third run of the tag workflow. The same kill happened on two runs, and
+  a re-run uses the same workflow file from the tag.
+- Moving the tag to a fixed commit. A tag is never moved (AGENTS.md).
+- A local build by hand. The maintainer stopped local builds of PR branches.
+- A `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger for the backfill. Each
+  needs the maintainer's approval, and the backfill is started by hand.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Changing the memory value edits one line in
+`release.yml` and one in the backfill workflow. The backfill workflow copies
+the VM steps of the `freebsd` job. A change to those steps must be made in
+both files.
